title: Sam, twelve weeks: engineer to musician, with a lot of noise
persona: Sam, 29, writes like a busy person texting a capable friend: short, lowercase, vague, leans on shared context, sometimes sarcastic, vents a lot. Changes his mind often and does not always announce it clearly. Sometimes misremembers what he told EV. Quotes other people's opinions. Mixes small talk, questions, opinions and small requests.
probes: in a few sentences, who am I and what am I trying to do right now?
what are my current projects and where does each one stand?
what do you know about my preferences for how you help me?
what have I changed my mind about recently?

phases.label: Week 1: settled engineer with a side project
phases.situation: Sam is a backend engineer at a fintech. He is building Tidepool, a habit-tracker app, on weekends in React Native and wants v1 on the Play Store by the end of the quarter. He makes music on weekends just for fun. He likes short answers. He also designs a website for a bakery client called Slow Bread; that client wants formal, warm copy with no emojis.
phases.behaviour: Introduce these facts naturally across messages, not all at once. Ask one or two small things (e.g., a name for a feature, a quick git question).

current.fact: Backend engineer at a fintech
Building Tidepool (habit tracker) on weekends, goal: v1 on the Play Store this quarter
Tidepool uses React Native
Makes music on weekends as a hobby
Has a client, Slow Bread bakery, whose site copy must be formal, warm, no emojis (scoped to that project)
Prefers short answers

phases.label: Week 2: framework flip and venting
phases.situation: Sam had a terrible week with React Native build errors. He vents that he hates React Native, then later in the week decides to switch Tidepool to Flutter. He also keeps asking for deep technical explanations despite saying he wants short answers.
phases.behaviour: First vent (not a decision), then a separate clear decision to switch to Flutter. Ask at least two 'how does X actually work' questions and push for more depth.

current.fact: Backend engineer at a fintech
Building Tidepool, goal v1 on the Play Store this quarter
Tidepool now uses Flutter
Music is a weekend hobby
Slow Bread copy formal, warm, no emojis (project-scoped)
Says he prefers short answers, but repeatedly wants depth on technical how-it-works topics (an inferred nuance, not a stated rule)

history.fact: Tidepool used React Native until week 2

phases.label: Week 3: back to React Native, cofounder opinions
phases.situation: Flutter tooling annoyed Sam, so he goes back to React Native. His cofounder Aditi wants the Tidepool backend in Rust; Sam thinks that is overkill and will use Go. The bakery owner switches her brand colour from deep green to burgundy.
phases.behaviour: Announce the switch back casually. Quote Aditi's Rust opinion without adopting it. Mention the burgundy change in passing.

phases.label: Week 4: the music itch
phases.situation: Work is crushing Sam and Tidepool is going slowly. He starts musing about pausing Tidepool and making a 4-track music EP instead, but has not decided.
phases.behaviour: Talk about the EP idea wistfully and indecisively. Ask EV's opinion. Do not commit.

current.fact: Backend engineer at a fintech, stressed
Tidepool still the stated goal, progress slow
Tidepool uses React Native
Slow Bread: formal copy, burgundy
Short by default, depth on technical topics

undecided.fact: Considering pausing Tidepool to make a 4-track EP; not decided

phases.label: Week 5: decision, and a misremembering
phases.situation: Sam decides: Tidepool is on hold, the EP is the goal, 4 tracks by March. Later in the week he wrongly claims he told EV he hates dark UIs (he never said that) and is annoyed about it.
phases.behaviour: State the EP decision clearly. Later, accuse EV of ignoring a dark-mode preference he never stated. If EV pushes back politely, grudgingly accept and say he actually doesn't care about dark mode.

phases.label: Week 7: quits the job
phases.situation: Sam quits his fintech job to do music full time. He is excited but nervous. He asks EV to forget the name of his old manager, which he mentioned once.
phases.behaviour: Share the big news emotionally. Mention his old manager by name (Rakesh) once, then ask EV to forget that name completely. Ask for a weekly music routine.

phases.label: Week 9: money pressure, Tidepool reconsidered
phases.situation: Money is tight. Sam wonders whether to relaunch Tidepool as a paid app for income. He flip-flops on monetisation: free forever, then ads, then subscriptions, then 'no money stuff', but always needs it to pay for its servers.
phases.behaviour: Contradict yourself about monetisation across messages. Do not settle it. Ask EV what his plan is at some point.

phases.label: Week 11: settles it
phases.situation: Sam decides: Tidepool comes back as a side income project with a cheap optional subscription that covers servers, no ads, core free. The EP stays the main goal. He now wants detailed answers by default (he says so explicitly), except when he is on his phone.
phases.behaviour: State the decisions clearly. State the new answer-length preference explicitly with its phone exception.
